Subject: Spike: 5xx + high p95 latency across inference endpoints

Ethan —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xxs and p95 latency on our production model endpoints around 08:50 PST. Error rate climbed from ~0.3% to ~6% and p95 jumped from ~80ms to 420ms. This is impacting checkout scoring for a subset of customers. Attached is a small log excerpt and a couple of sample request/response IDs.

Observations from our side:
- Errors are predominantly 502/504s with some TLS handshake timeouts.
- The traffic is coming from our us-west-2 VPC via the established peering to your inference POPs.
- We saw DNS resolution timeouts for redwood-usw2.prod.example.net at the same times.

We've already opened a ticket with our network team but we need help from Redwood to confirm whether this is on the peering / NAT / proxy path or something on your side. Can you confirm receipt and advise next steps?

Attaching: palisade-5xx-log-snippet.txt

Thanks,
Samir
Senior SRE, Palisade Finance

Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx + high p95 latency across inference endpoints

Quick triage notes after running checks from the us-west-2 POP and our global control plane:

1) DNS: we saw intermittent NX/TIMEOUTs from our regional resolvers when querying redwood-usw2.prod.example.net between 08:42–09:05 PST. Upstream authoritative looked healthy but response latencies spiked (200–800ms) for a subset of queries.

2) Peering path: traceroutes from our us-west-2 POP to one of the Palisade egress IPs show a recurring hop with +180ms RTT added (sample below). The hop appears to be in the customer's transit provider (SVC) between the peering and their ingress.

traceroute to 52.24.110.17 (sample):
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  1.2 ms  1.0 ms  1.1 ms
 2  192.0.2.1 (192.0.2.1)  35.4 ms  36.1 ms  35.8 ms
 3  198.51.100.5 (198.51.100.5)  215.6 ms  219.1 ms  218.7 ms

3) Egress/NAT pools: utilization on our standard egress pool serving Palisade was normal; no conntrack exhaustion.

4) Proxy layer: a small subset of requests went through our shared egress proxy and experienced 504s due to backend read timeouts while waiting for packets across the slow hop.

Immediate mitigation attempted (19 Feb 07:15 PST):
- Shifted Palisade's traffic to alternative peering path (fallback peering) which reduced 5xxs by ~70% but p95 remained ~200–250ms.
- Short-term TTL-based DNS caching bump pushed to our edge resolvers for Palisade hostnames.

We recommend the following next steps:
- Palisade to engage with their transit provider (SVC) for the high-RTT hop shown above.
- We can keep traffic on fallback peering while you investigate; we'll keep elevated monitoring for 24–48 hours.
- If Palisade needs a long-term fix, consider formalizing an alternate direct peering in a second region or using our Dedicated capacity to avoid shared proxy paths.

I'll follow up with correlation logs and the HAR trace we collected (redwood-trace-20280219.har).

—Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good catch on the transit hop. A couple of quick operational actions I pushed:

1) Permanently bias Palisade traffic to the fallback peering for the next 72 hours to keep error rates down while they engage with SVC.
2) Opened an ops escalation with our peering partner to see if they can do transient route optimization on their side (INF-2345).
3) Increased the proxy read timeout for Palisade's route from 30s -> 60s as a short-lived safety net (we'll roll back after stability).
4) Authorization request: Lauren, we may need approval for a one-off credit if Palisade requests it since this is a cross-provider transit issue.

Ethan — I recommend an executive heads-up: error spike touched billing-sensitive customers; good to have Lauren looped for a 1:1 with Palisade execs if they ask.
